title: In 1878, a Cloud of Flour Dust Blew Up Six Flour Mills

scenes.text: In 1878, flour exploded and flattened six mills.
Minneapolis. May second. Around seven in the evening.
A spark lit the flour dust floating in the air.
Eighteen people died. Some stone landed eight city blocks away.
People in Saint Paul, ten miles away, heard it. Some thought it was an earthquake.
Flour is food. A cloud of it is a bomb.

description:
On 2 May 1878 a flour dust explosion at the Washburn A Mill in Minneapolis destroyed the mill and the mills beside it, six in all, and killed 18 people.
Investigators believed two dry millstones created a spark that lit the suspended flour dust. The blast was heard ten miles away in Saint Paul.
Did you know flour could explode? Tell us.
first_comment: Grain dust and flour dust explosions still happen in factories today. Did you ever try the flame-and-flour demo at school?
